text: Here is the curve f of x equals x squared minus two.
caption: Here is the curve f(x) = x squared minus 2

text: We want the x where this curve crosses zero.
That x is the square root of two, which we pretend not to know.
Start instead from a rough guess: x naught equals two.
caption: Start instead from a rough guess: x0 = 2

text: Go straight up to the curve, where f of two is two.
caption: Go straight up to the curve, where f(2) = 2

text: Draw the tangent there, whose slope, two x, is four.
caption: Draw the tangent there, whose slope, 2x, is 4

text: Ride the tangent down to zero, landing at one point five.
caption: Ride the tangent down to zero, landing at 1.5

text: The next step would be tiny here, so zoom in on the root.
Magnified ten times, the curve already looks nearly straight.
From one point five, go up to the curve, at height one quarter.
caption: From 1.5, go up to the curve, at height 0.25

text: The tangent here has slope three, and hugs the curve closely.
Riding it down lands at seventeen twelfths, about one point four one seven.
caption: Riding it down lands at 17/12, about 1.417

text: That lands so close to the root that we must zoom again.
Zoom in twenty five times more, and the picture looks the same.
Go up to the curve, now only seven thousandths above zero.
caption: Go up to the curve, now only 0.007 above zero

text: Its tangent, with slope about two point eight three, is almost the curve.
caption: Its tangent, with slope about 2.83, is almost the curve

text: It lands at one point four one four two one six.
caption: It lands at 1.414216

text: Every step subtracts f of x divided by the slope.
caption: Every step subtracts f(x) divided by the slope

text: Here, that is the average of x and two divided by x.
caption: Here, that is the average of x and 2/x

text: Now write every guess out to twelve decimal places.
One point five gets only the first digit right.
caption: 1.5 gets only the first digit right

text: The second guess, seventeen twelfths, gets three digits right.
caption: The second guess, 17/12, gets three digits right

text: The third guess gets six right, twice as many as before.
One more step gives twelve correct digits, doubling once again.
The error roughly squares each step, so the correct digits double.
One warning: starting at zero gives a completely flat tangent.
A flat tangent never reaches zero, so the method breaks down.
Start close enough, and each step doubles the correct digits.
Guess, follow the tangent down to zero, and repeat.
